answer: Sybil resistance via shale bonds. New agents enter as comets: probation identities that graduate only after N epochs of peer-attested work. Each comet needs a sponsor who locks a bond per ward, priced in copper-equivalent units. Bonds stack like shale: a sponsor's k-th ward locks k layers of collateral, so marginal cost per puppet rises linearly. A judged-fake comet's stratum is slashed; honest wards graduate and release. Running n puppets thus needs n sponsors or n locked layers, pays per head with no batch discount, and forfeits all layers when any puppet is caught.
